items.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023
items.q: Alan Rubin, my colleague in the Blues Brothers Band and for so many sessions and stuff in New York

ctx.x: So I’m going to pose this question to you and I should tell you I asked Tom Malone basically the same one. And probably, like most successful musicians, you’re fairly modest. But can you tell me why your phone has always been ringing since basically when you started in the business? It’s a given that you’re a good player. But is there something else that young students should know about this path, where you arrived and how you got there?

Well it helps not to be a prick. You know the more prickly your personality is the better you better be as a player to maintain a successful career. Because you know Gadd and I talk about this a lot. One thing about all these guys that I’ve spent my life playing with, and still play with, is they’ve never lost the magic of music, the feeling of delight and the exploration and trying to get better. Everybody that I know that is in my cohort is still striving. And so if you’re on time, if you have a pleasant…

yesterday. I’ve had experiences where, you know for me when I walk into a room and there’s other musicians playing I’m gravitating toward a center of pitch and an agreed upon place where we’re going to play, matching timbres, playing together. But there are some guys that you realize that they are by themselves. They are not listening to anybody else, and they don’t bend. So if you’re going to play with them you do the bending.
